title: Continuous coefficient sections across a normal principal open
statement:
Let $Q$ be a commutative normal ring, meaning that each prime localization is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $s\in Q$ have injective multiplication on $Q$, put $X=\operatorname{Spec}Q$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $i:X_s=\operatorname{Spec}Q[1/s]\hookrightarrow X$ be the principal open immersion, where localization is [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Let $E$ be a nonarchimedean normed field, meaning that its absolute value satisfies $|a+b|\leq\max(|a|,|b|)$, with its metric topology. Define the commutative condensed ring $C_E(P)=C(P,E)$ on profinite sets using all continuous maps, and its coefficient sheaves $C_{E,Z}=p_Z^*C_E$ on small pro-etale sites [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Then inverse image induces a bijection on clopen subsets and a homeomorphism
$$h:\pi_0(X_s)\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_0(X),\qquad hq_{X_s}=q_Xi,$$
where $\pi_0$ is the set of connected components with the quotient topology and $q$ is the component projection. Actual restriction induces ring bijections
$$C(|X|,E)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(|X_s|,E),\qquad
\Gamma(X,C_{E,X})\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X_s,C_{E,X_s}).$$
Under the canonical continuous-function realization [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-field-continuous-realization] these are the same map. The inverse on functions sends $a=\bar a q_{X_s}$ to $\bar a h^{-1}q_X$. For every scheme $Z$ and affine pro-etale object $X\to Z$, the same coefficient bijection holds for evaluation of $C_{E,Z}$ on $X$ and $X_s$. These bijections and their inverses are natural for every morphism $v:X'\to X$ between such normal affine pairs with $v^{-1}(X_s)=X'_{s'}$: restriction commutes with precomposition by $v$ and $v|_{X'_{s'}}$. No Noetherian or integral-domain assumption on $Q$ is imposed. The zero ring and $s=1$ are included.

source.place: Agent consequence of Tag 034M (lemma-normal-ring-integrally-closed), via clopen idempotents; Bhatt–Scholze, The pro-etale topology for schemes, Lemma 4.2.12, and Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach, Constructible sheaves on schemes, Example 3.1. Extracts returned parent proof steps 2–5; not a verbatim Stacks assertion.

proof.text: Write $K=S^{-1}Q$ for the total fraction ring, where $S$ is the set of nonzerodivisors. The fraction relations in [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] give injections $Q\to Q[1/s]\to K$: every power of $s$ is regular, and if $u a=0$ for $u\in S$, then $a=0$. Thus we may regard both rings as subrings of $K$. An idempotent $b\in Q[1/s]$ satisfies the monic equation $b^2-b=0$ in $K$, hence is integral by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. By [lem-weil-pbc-normal-ring-integrally-closed-total] it is the image of some $e\in Q$. Injectivity gives $e^2=e$ and uniqueness. Conversely every idempotent of $Q$ remains idempotent after localization. Hence localization induces a bijection on idempotents.

source.place: Tag 034M, lemma-normal-ring-integrally-closed; elementary fraction calculation and monic equation

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] to $Q$ and $Q[1/s]$. The clopen attached to $e$ is $D(e)$. A prime of $Q[1/s]$ contains the image of $e$ exactly when its contracted prime contains $e$, so $i^{-1}D(e)=D(e/1)$. The bijection on idempotents of step 1 therefore identifies actual inverse image on clopens with a bijection.

source.place: Tag 00EE, lemma-disjoint-decomposition; inverse image under prime contraction

proof.text: Both $X$ and $X_s$ are affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and their underlying spaces are spectral by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral]. Apply [lem-sfb-spectral-clopen-component-homeomorphism] to the continuous map $i$ and the clopen bijection of step 2. This gives precisely $h:\pi_0(X_s)\cong\pi_0(X)$ with $hq_{X_s}=q_Xi$, using the quotient topologies stipulated in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0906, lemma-spectral-pi0; clopen criterion supplied by the cited existing node

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-ultrametric-component-map-extension] with $Y=|X_s|$, $Z=|X|$, $A=E$, and the normalized $i,h$ of step 3. Its hypotheses require exactly the stated nonarchimedean absolute value. It gives total disconnectedness of $E$, the unique continuous factor $a=\bar a q_{X_s}$, and the ring bijection given by actual restriction, with inverse $a\mapsto\bar a h^{-1}q_X$. No compactness or completeness hypothesis on $E$ is used.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, component factorization; existing ultrametric extension tool

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-field-continuous-realization], the totally disconnected normed field $E$ has its canonical ring-sheaf realization by continuous functions. Its normalization is the comparison of [def-sfb-continuous-ring-canonical-comparison]. The scheme-pullback equation of [lem-sfb-normalized-continuous-set-comparison-coherence], applied to its underlying set sheaves, says that this comparison intertwines the point-pullback coefficient identification and precomposition on functions. Thus the actual coefficient restriction for $i$ is the function restriction in step 4, and is bijective. Applying the same realization on any $Z$, its evaluation at objects $X\to Z$ and $X_s\to Z$ is $C(|X|,E)\to C(|X_s|,E)$ with exactly this restriction. The normalization hypotheses of the coherence node hold because both comparisons are defined by the same profinite-test adjunct equations; its sheaf hypotheses hold by the ring-sheaf realization.

source.place: Example 3.1 and following scheme-pullback paragraph, p.6; normalized comparison equation

proof.text: For a morphism of pairs $v:X\prime\to X$, let $v_s:X\prime_{s\prime}\to X_s$ be its restriction. The equality $vi\prime=iv_s$ gives $(g\circ v)\circ i\prime=(g\circ i)\circ v_s$. This proves naturality of restriction. If $E_X$ and $E_{X\prime}$ denote the inverses constructed in step 4, both $E_X(a)\circ v$ and $E_{X\prime}(a\circ v_s)$ restrict to $a\circ v_s$; injectivity for $X\prime$ makes them equal. Step 5 transports these equalities to coefficients. If $Q=0$, both spectra are empty, their component spaces and clopen sets are empty and singleton respectively, and the function and section rings have one element. If $s=1$, all maps are identities. Each preceding argument also includes these cases.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q101-ab8941d26 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the statement, all 6 steps and all 12 cited statements; the delivery adds no new nodes and keeps the base statement. Sources: Stacks algebra.tex 034M (normal rings are integrally closed in the total ring of fractions, with no minimal-prime hypothesis) and topology.tex lemma-spectral-pi0. Step 1: s regular makes Q→Q[1/s]→K injective; the monic t²−t and 034M give the idempotent bijection. Step 2: i⁻¹D(e)=D(e/1) plus the clopen-idempotent leaf gives a clopen bijection. Step 3: affine⇒qcqs⇒spectral, then the spectral clopen-component lemma gives h with hq_{X_s}=q_X i. Step 4: ultrametric component-extension, hypotheses matched, inverse formula identical. Step 5: realization (totally disconnected E from step 4) plus the coherence pullback square with D=E (Hausdorff, totally disconnected; normalization r_{X,S}=π_S) conjugate coefficient restriction to precomposition, and the Z-evaluation clause follows from naturality of the sheaf isomorphism. Step 6: naturality by injectivity, and the Q=0 and s=1 cases hold. Tested: k[x] with s=x, Z with s=2, k×k with s=(1,0) (non-regular, excluded), and the non-normal k[x,y]/(xy) with s=x+y, which disconnects the axes, so normality is needed. Duplicate search found nothing (punctured-idempotent-complement is a different statement). No cycle, no SGA. Accepted tool_uses: normal-ring-integrally-closed-total and condensed-field-continuous-realization (both generic). Advisory: step 5's move from ring-level p_X^* to set-level σ is elementary (left-exact inverse images commute with the forgetful functor).
